## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The helper behaves correctly for ASCII titles, but it removes accented and non-Latin letters even though the description says it only replaces non-alphanumeric characters. The pull-request description also breaks a contributor rule.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/slug.py:7 — correctness — The pattern `[^a-z0-9]+` only keeps ASCII letters and digits, so it treats letters like `é` and `日` as separators. `slugify("Crème brûlée")` returns `"cr-me-br-l-e"`, and `slugify("日本語")` returns `""`. The PR description says it "replaces runs of non-alphanumeric characters", and in Python those letters count as alphanumeric (`str.isalnum()`). Should titles be transliterated first (for example, `unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", ...)` and then dropping combining marks), or should the description say the slug keeps ASCII only? Either way, please add a non-ASCII case to `tests/test_slug.py`. — Pages with non-English titles get garbled URLs, and every title written entirely in a non-Latin script gets the same empty slug, so their URLs collide.
- PR body — correctness — The description has no `## Testing` section. AGENTS.md:4 says: "Every pull-request description has a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified." Could you add one that says how the slug tests were run? — The PR breaks a contributor rule, and reviewers can't tell how the change was checked.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- Both new modules start with a docstring that says what they are for, as AGENTS.md:3 requires.
- The parametrized tests cover runs of repeated hyphens, leading and trailing whitespace and hyphens, a title made only of separators, and an empty string.
